lines: Title: Summation from k to m of r Choose k by s Choose n-k by nr-(r+s)k
:$\ds \sum_{k \mathop = 0}^m \dbinom r k \dbinom s {n - k} \paren {n r - \paren {r + s} k} = \paren {m + 1} \paren {n - m} \dbinom r {m + 1} \dbinom s {n - m}$
The proof proceeds by [[Principle of Mathematical Induction|induction]] over $m$.
:$\ds \sum_{k \mathop = 0}^m \dbinom r k \dbinom s {n - k} \paren {n r - \paren {r + s} k} = \paren {m + 1} \paren {n - m} \dbinom r {m + 1} \dbinom s {n - m}$
{{eqn | l = \sum_{k \mathop = 0}^0 \dbinom r k \dbinom s {n - k} \paren {n r - \paren {r + s} k}
Thus $\map P 0$ is seen to hold.
This is the [[Definition:Basis for the Induction|basis for the induction]].
Now it needs to be shown that, if $\map P j$ is true, where $j \ge 1$, then it logically follows that $\map P {j + 1}$ is true.
So this is the [[Definition:Induction Hypothesis|induction hypothesis]]:
:$\ds \sum_{k \mathop = 0}^j \dbinom r k \dbinom s {n - k} \paren {n r - \paren {r + s} k} = \paren {j + 1} \paren {n - j} \dbinom r {j + 1} \dbinom s {n - j}$
from which it is to be shown that:
:$\ds \sum_{k \mathop = 0}^{j + 1} \dbinom r k \dbinom s {n - k} \paren {n r - \paren {r + s} k} = \paren {j + 2} \paren {n - j - 1} \dbinom r {j + 2} \dbinom s {n - j - 1}$
{{eqn | r = \sum_{k \mathop = 0}^{j + 1} \dbinom r k \dbinom s {n - k} \paren {n r - \paren {r + s} k}
{{eqn | r = \sum_{k \mathop = 0}^j \dbinom r k \dbinom s {n - k} \paren {n r - \paren {r + s} k} + \dbinom r {j + 1} \dbinom s {n - j - 1} \paren {n r - \paren {r + s} \paren {j + 1} }
{{eqn | r = \paren {j + 1} \paren {n - j} \dbinom r {j + 1} \dbinom s {n - j} + \dbinom r {j + 1} \dbinom s {n - j - 1} \paren {n r - \paren {r + s} \paren {j + 1} }
{{eqn | r = \dbinom r {j + 1} \paren {\paren {j + 1} \paren {n - j} \dbinom s {n - j} + \dbinom s {n - j - 1} \paren {n r - \paren {r + s} \paren {j + 1} } }
{{eqn | r = \paren {j + 2} \paren {r - j + 2} \dbinom r {j + 2} \paren {\paren {j + 1} \paren {n - j} \dbinom s {n - j} + \dbinom s {n - j - 1} \paren {n r - \paren {r + s} \paren {j + 1} } }

{{eqn | r = \paren {j + 2} \paren {r - j + 2} \dbinom r {j + 2} \paren {\dfrac {\paren {j + 1} \paren {n - j} } {\paren {n - j} \paren {s - \paren {n - j} } } \dbinom s {n - j - 1} + \dbinom s {n - j - 1} \paren {n r - \paren {r + s} \paren {j + 1} } }
{{eqn | r = \paren {j + 2} \paren {r - j + 2} \dbinom r {j + 2} \dbinom s {n - j - 1} \paren {\dfrac {j + 1} {s - n + j} + \paren {n r - \paren {r + s} \paren {j + 1} } }
{{eqn | r = \paren {j + 2} \paren {r - j + 2} \dbinom r {j + 2} \dbinom s {n - j - 1} \paren {\dfrac {j + 1} {s - n + j} + \paren {n r - r j - s j - r - s} }
So $\map P j \implies \map P {j + 1}$ and the result follows by the [[Principle of Mathematical Induction]].
:$\ds \sum_{k \mathop = 0}^m \dbinom r k \dbinom s {n - k} \paren {n r - \paren {r + s} k} = \paren {m + 1} \paren {n - m} \dbinom r {m + 1} \dbinom s {n - m}$
